title: Advisory Locks vs FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED for Message Queues
realWorldScenario: You are building a background task processor where multiple worker processes concurrently poll an `outbox_events` table to process and publish pending events. Standard `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` causes workers to block each other and serialize execution.
questionStatement: Compare `SELECT FOR UPDATE`, `SELECT FOR UPDATE NOWAIT`, and `SELECT FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`. Write a concurrency-safe worker query that claims exactly 5 unprocessed events, locks them so no other worker can touch them, and updates their status to `PROCESSING` in an atomic transaction.
starterCode:
-- Concurrently safe job queue claim query
WITH claimed_jobs AS (
    SELECT id
    FROM outbox_events
    WHERE status = 'PENDING'
    ORDER BY id ASC
    LIMIT 5
    FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED
)
UPDATE outbox_events
SET 
    status = 'PROCESSING',
    processed_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
FROM claimed_jobs
WHERE outbox_events.id = claimed_jobs.id
RETURNING outbox_events.id, outbox_events.payload, outbox_events.status;
expectedConcepts: FOR UPDATE blocking behavior vs NOWAIT failure
SKIP LOCKED silently bypassing locked rows for parallel worker queues
CTE pairing SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED with UPDATE ... RETURNING
Index requirement on (status, id) to avoid sequential scan locking
hints: SKIP LOCKED skips rows that are currently locked by other transactions.
Wrap the SELECT in a CTE to feed the IDs directly into an UPDATE statement.
Use RETURNING to fetch the job payload in the same round-trip.

testCases.description: Verify CTE update with claimed status
testCases.setupSql:
CREATE TABLE outbox_events (id INT PRIMARY KEY, status VARCHAR(20), payload VARCHAR(50), processed_at VARCHAR(30));
INSERT INTO outbox_events VALUES (1, 'PENDING', 'event_1', NULL), (2, 'PENDING', 'event_2', NULL), (3, 'DONE', 'event_3', '2026-01-01');
testCases.expectedOutputSql: UPDATE outbox_events SET status = 'PROCESSING' WHERE status = 'PENDING'; SELECT id, status, payload FROM outbox_events WHERE status = 'PROCESSING' ORDER BY id;
